The 30-year mortgage rate dipped again this week — and it's still stuck above 7%.

Freddie Mac says the average 30-year fixed eased to 7.21%, down from 7.28% the week before — a saving of about $19 a month on a typical new loan. The 15-year fixed is 6.54%.

Here's the catch: rates have sat above 7% since September, and a 7-basis-point move barely changes a payment. Pending home sales just hit their slowest October since 2018, per the National Association of Realtors — buyers are frozen.

My take: a 7-basis-point dip on a 7% rate is a rounding error. Until that number starts with a 5, the affordability math doesn't change for most buyers.

Are today's rates keeping you out of the housing market? 👇

Source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (week of Nov. 25, 2026); NAR pending home sales
